questions.stem: Find the volume of a cube whose side is 5 cm.

options.option_text: 125 cm³ (correct: volume of cube = side³ = 5³ = 125 cm³ ✓)

questions.explanation: C is correct. Volume of cube = a³ = 5³ = 125 cm³. Total surface area = 6a² = 6×25 = 150 cm² (common distractor). Don't confuse volume (a³) with surface area (6a²).

questions.stem: A cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. What is its volume? (Use π = 22/7)

options.option_text: 770 cm³ (half of correct answer — forgot height or halved wrongly)
440 cm³ (curved surface area = 2πrh = 2×22/7×7×10 = 440 — confused volume with CSA)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Volume of cylinder = πr²h = (22/7) × 7² × 10 = (22/7) × 49 × 10 = 22 × 7 × 10 = 1540 cm³. **Short Trick:** r=7 cancels the 7 in 22/7: (22 × 7 × h) = 22 × 7 × 10 = 1540.

questions.stem: The total surface area of a cuboid is 2(lb + bh + lh). Find the TSA of a cuboid with l=8 cm, b=5 cm, h=3 cm.
questions.explanation: D is correct. TSA of cuboid = 2(lb+bh+lh) = 2(8×5 + 5×3 + 8×3) = 2(40+15+24) = 2×79 = 158 cm². Volume = lbh = 8×5×3 = 120 cm³ (a common distractor in TSA questions).

questions.stem: A sphere has radius 6 cm. What is its volume? (Use π = 22/7)

options.option_text: 288π cm³ (without substituting π — but the question asks with π=22/7)

questions.stem: If the radius of a sphere is doubled, by what factor does its volume increase?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³. When radius doubles: new volume = (4/3)π(2r)³ = (4/3)π×8r³ = 8 × original volume. Volume scales as the cube of the linear dimension. Factor = 2³ = 8.

questions.stem: A cone has base radius 3 cm and height 4 cm. What is its slant height?

options.option_text: 5 cm (correct: l=√(r²+h²)=√(9+16)=√25=5 cm — a 3-4-5 Pythagorean triple ✓)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Slant height l = √(r²+h²) = √(3²+4²) = √(9+16) = √25 = 5 cm. This is the classic 3-4-5 Pythagorean triple. Memorise these triples: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25.

questions.stem: A metallic cube of side 4 cm is melted and recast into a cylinder of height 8 cm. What is the radius of the cylinder? (Use π = 22/7)

options.option_text: 2 cm (wrong: would give cylinder vol=4×22/7×8 — not 64)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Volume conserved: cube vol = πr²h. 4³ = (22/7)×r²×8. 64 = (176/7)×r². r² = 64×7/176 = 448/176 = 28/11. r = √(28/11) cm. This tests the key principle: volume is preserved when metal is recast.

questions.stem: A hollow cylindrical pipe is 14 m long. Its outer radius is 5 cm and inner radius is 4 cm. Find the volume of the metal used (in cm³). (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: B is correct. Length = 14 m = 1400 cm. Volume of hollow cylinder = π(R²−r²)×h = (22/7)×(5²−4²)×1400 = (22/7)×9×1400 = 22×9×200 = 39600 cm³. Key: convert units consistently (14m = 1400 cm); use π(R²−r²) for hollow cross-section.

questions.stem: A hemispherical bowl has inner radius 6 cm. How many litres of water can it hold? (1 L = 1000 cm³, π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: A is correct. Volume of hemisphere = (2/3)πr³ = (2/3)×(22/7)×216 = (2×22×216)/21 = 9504/21 ≈ 452.57 cm³. In litres: 452.57/1000 ≈ 0.453 L ≈ 0.452 L. Hemisphere = half sphere; use (2/3)πr³ instead of (4/3)πr³.

questions.stem: The curved surface area of a cone with radius 7 cm and slant height 10 cm is:

options.option_text: 154 cm² (base area only: πr²=(22/7)×49=154 — not CSA)
374 cm² (total surface area: 220+154=374 — that's TSA, not CSA)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Curved Surface Area of cone = πrl = (22/7) × 7 × 10 = 22 × 10 = 220 cm². Note: r=7 cancels the 7 in denominator. Total Surface Area (TSA) = πrl + πr² = 220 + 154 = 374 cm². CSA ≠ TSA.

questions.stem: Water flows through a pipe of diameter 3.5 cm at 2 m/s. How many litres flow per minute? (π = 22/7; 1 L = 1000 cm³)

options.option_text: 1.925 L/min (volume per second instead of per minute)

questions.explanation: B is correct. r = 3.5/2 = 1.75 cm. Cross-section area = π×(1.75)² = (22/7)×3.0625 = 9.625 cm². Speed = 2 m/s = 200 cm/s. Volume per second = 9.625×200 = 1925 cm³/s. Per minute = 1925×60 = 115500 cm³ = 115.5 litres.

questions.stem: A rectangular tank 10 m long, 5 m wide, and 3 m deep is filled with water. If water is pumped out at 20 litres/second, how many minutes does it take to empty the tank? (1 m³ = 1000 L)

options.option_text: 75 minutes (correct: volume=10×5×3=150 m³=150000 L; time=150000/20=7500 s=125 min — wait: 7500/60=125 min)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Volume = 10×5×3 = 150 m³ = 150,000 litres. Pump rate = 20 L/s. Time = 150000/20 = 7500 seconds = 7500/60 = 125 minutes.
